children: SYDNEY--Australian services activity continued to expand in September, but at the slowest pace in three months.
The seasonally adjusted S&P Global Australia Services PMI business activity index stood at 51.9 in September, down from 53.2 in August.
"The services sector remained in expansion territory in September, in contrast to the deepening contraction in the manufacturing sector," said Jingyi Pan, economist at S&P Global Market Intelligence.
Falling confidence among service providers meanwhile hinted at the likelihood that growth could wane further, she added.
Firms have been battling headwinds of rising fuel costs, geopolitical risks and a rise in interest rates locally to their highest level in 15 years.
While the economy continues to grow, weak productivity growth means that even modest rates of expansion are generating inflation pressures.
Elevated price pressures in the service sector do not bode well for demand recovery as growth in services new business softened for the second month in a row, Pan said.
Softer growth of new orders led to a resumption of job shedding as companies looked to limit costs, while business confidence also declined, she added.
"Acceleration of output price inflation in the private sector suggests that inflation could remain elevated in the coming months, which could keep policy makers on a hawkish bias," Pan said.

title: Australian Services Sector Expansion Cools in September
